changes.old:
Estimates the skeleton of a character, returning a list of keypoints to use with the skeleton animation tool.

Supported image sizes: 
- 16x16
- 32x32
- 64x64
- 128x128
- 256x256

Using the Python client:
```python
import pixellab

client = pixellab.Client(secret="YOUR_API_TOKEN")

response = client.estimate_skeleton(
    image=image_of_the_character_on_a_transparent_background,
)
response.keypoints
```
changes.new:
Estimates the skeleton of a character, returning a list of keypoints to use with the skeleton animation tool.

Any image size up to 256x256 works. The model runs on 16/32/64/128/256 squares, so an
image of another size is padded to the next one that fits and the returned coordinates
are converted back — `x`/`y` are fractions 0-1 of the image YOU sent, not of the padded
square, so they can be passed straight to the skeleton animation endpoints. A 40x40 or
56x56 sprite therefore needs no padding from you.

Cost: 0.1 generations per call. A fully transparent image is refused (422) before it is
charged, since there is no character to estimate from.

Using the Python client:
```python
import pixellab

client = pixellab.Client(secret="YOUR_API_TOKEN")

response = client.estimate_skeleton(
    image=image_of_the_character_on_a_transparent_background,
)
response.keypoints
```

changes.old:
Beta. Animate a sprite by posing it: one skeleton per frame, drawn from a single reference image.

Returns immediately with a background job ID. Poll `GET /v2/background-jobs/{job_id}`
to retrieve results when generation completes.

**How it works:**
1. Send the sprite, the skeleton of the pose it is already in (`first_frame_keypoints`), and one skeleton per frame you want (`keypoints`).
2. Poll `GET /v2/background-jobs/{background_job_id}` every 5-10 seconds.
3. When `status` is `completed`, `last_response.images` holds exactly `len(keypoints)` frames, each the size of `first_frame`. The reference frame is not returned.

**Skeletons:** 18 humanoid joints, `x`/`y` as fractions 0-1 of the image. `depth` is
optional -- leave it out and it is taken from the standing pose of `template_id` for
your direction, which is what an editor without 3D data should do. `GET /v2/estimate-skeleton`
will derive a skeleton from an image if you do not have one.

**Limits:** 3-15 frames, canvas up to 256x256.

**Cost:** by generation time, which depends on frame count and not on canvas size:
3 frames = 2 generations,
8 frames = 3,
15 frames = 4. A longer clip
is nearly free, so prefer one long clip to several short ones.

Typical generation time: 3-5 minutes.

changes.old: Animation mode. "template": skeleton-based from template_animation_id (1 gen/direction; canvases over ~100px run in batches billed 1 each, up to one per clip frame at 256px). "skeleton-v3": the same template_animation_id posed onto the character, which moves the character instead of redrawing it each frame — steadier identity and colours, 2-4 generations and ~3-5 min per direction, beta. "v3": custom animation from action_description with frame_count control. "pixminimax": custom animation from action_description on PixMiniMax (beta) — up to 40 frames at any size, priced by size and frame count (64x64 at 8 frames = 1 generation, 40 frames = 6), ~1-7 min per direction. "pro" (legacy, prefer v3 or pixminimax): custom animation that generates directions sequentially, using completed sides as reference (10-25 gen/direction). Auto-detected: template if template_animation_id is provided, v3 otherwise.
changes.new: Animation mode. "template": skeleton-based from template_animation_id (1 gen/direction; canvases over ~100px run in batches billed 1 each, up to one per clip frame at 256px). "skeleton-v3": the same template_animation_id posed onto the character, which moves the character instead of redrawing it each frame — steadier identity and colours, 2-4 generations and ~3-5 min per direction, beta. Without template_animation_id, "skeleton-v3" animates action_description instead: the action is written into one 3D motion (3-15 frames, ~15 s before the jobs start) that every direction of the animation is drawn from, so directions added later with animation_group_id move the same way (humanoid characters). "v3": custom animation from action_description with frame_count control. "pixminimax": custom animation from action_description on PixMiniMax (beta) — up to 40 frames at any size, priced by size and frame count (64x64 at 8 frames = 1 generation, 40 frames = 6), ~1-7 min per direction. "pro" (legacy, prefer v3 or pixminimax): custom animation that generates directions sequentially, using completed sides as reference (10-25 gen/direction). Auto-detected: template if template_animation_id is provided, v3 otherwise.

changes.old: Number of animation frames. v3 mode: 4-16, even. pixminimax mode: a multiple of 4 from 4 to 40. Not used in other modes.
changes.new: Number of animation frames. v3 mode: 4-16, even. pixminimax mode: a multiple of 4 from 4 to 40. skeleton-v3 with action_description: 3-15 (a later direction of the same animation keeps the animation's own count). Not used in other modes.

changes.old: Colours the result must use and/or a colour cap: {"colors": ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"], "name": "Game Boy", "max_colors": 4}. With colors every pixel of every frame of every direction (modes pro, v3 and pixminimax; the character's frame goes onto the palette first; give colors: a max_colors cap alone would pick different colours for each direction) is one of them; max_colors (2-64) caps the colours of every frame of every direction (modes pro, v3 and pixminimax; the character's frame goes onto the palette first; give colors: a max_colors cap alone would pick different colours for each direction).
changes.new: Colours the result must use and/or a colour cap: {"colors": ["#081820", "#346856", "#88c070", "#e0f8d0"], "name": "Game Boy", "max_colors": 4}. With colors every pixel of every frame of every direction (modes pro, v3, pixminimax and skeleton-v3; the character's frame goes onto the palette first; give colors: a max_colors cap alone would pick different colours for each direction) is one of them; max_colors (2-64) caps the colours of every frame of every direction (modes pro, v3, pixminimax and skeleton-v3; the character's frame goes onto the palette first; give colors: a max_colors cap alone would pick different colours for each direction).

changes.old: Body type for skeleton reconstruction. Picks the 3D template the skeleton estimator fits to the generated frames so the character can be animated. Use `mannequin` for bipedal subjects or one of `bear`/`cat`/`dog`/`horse`/`lion` for quadrupeds. Must match the body type in `reference_image`.
changes.new: Body type for skeleton reconstruction. Picks the 3D template the skeleton estimator fits to the generated frames so the character can be animated. Use `mannequin` for bipedal subjects or one of `bear`/`cat`/`dog`/`horse`/`lion` for quadrupeds. Must match the body type in `reference_image`. `custom` skips the skeleton, for bodies no template fits; such a character can't use skeleton-based animations.
